tagline: Thailand's royal resort coast — anchor of the cross-Gulf line.
summary: Hua Hin is Thailand's historic royal-resort coast in Prachuap Khiri Khan — a 15 km sweep of white sand, high-end resorts and a relaxed atmosphere ~2.5-3hr south of Bangkok. It anchors the Royal Coast cluster (with Cha-Am ~14 nm north) and the marquee cross-Gulf line: a Hua Hin<->Pattaya ferry already exists under a government-backed project because the ~58 nm crossing halves the 5-6hr road loop around the head of the Gulf. It runs on slow diesel and is chronically suspended in swell — exactly the gap a foiling tier closes, and the crossing fits Pioneer II today.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The cross-Gulf Hua Hin<->Pattaya line (~58 nm) and the Hua Hin<->Cha-Am coastal hop (~14 nm) are both all-electric Pioneer II legs; berth-pedestal charging at the Hua Hin front.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Not required for the near-term build — every Royal Coast leg fits the all-electric boat. Quanta-LR is reserved for any future long-horizon lower-Gulf extension.

competitive_landscape: The cross-Gulf route is served by a slow, government-backed diesel ferry that is chronically suspended in swell; the coastal leg has no water option at all. Reliability and a premium tier are the open gaps — the demand is already proven.
seasonality: Peak: Nov-Apr cool/dry. The upper Gulf is rougher in the SW monsoon; foiling above the chop extends the comfortable, reliable operating window the diesel ferry lacks.
regulatory_note: Thai Marine Department licensing; the existing cross-Gulf ferry runs under a government-backed framework (East-West Ferry Project / Royal Passenger Liner), a friendly precedent for a premium successor.
